evidence: Read cold, task/instruction.md is a first-person product ask from a small firm with a motivating problem and priorities, not a spec: line 1 'Kittle & Rowe is a small law firm, and our clients keep emailing documents to whoever answered last. We want a secure chat where each client talks to us inside their legal matter...'; line 3 'Two things matter more than anything else. First, ethical walls... Second, retention...'; line 9 'Before you hand it over, please try it the way we'll use it: sign in as different people, post, reply, edit, search and open a transcript, and make sure nothing breaks.' It contains no numbered acceptance list, no shall/must table, no feature matrix, no framework/endpoint/file-layout recipe. The only paths (line 5: /assets/seed_data.json, /instructions, /app, /app/server.js, /app/app.db) are the template-required deliverable/runtime contract stated in one plain sentence, not a build recipe. The referenced notes keep the same voice and give reasons with each rule rather than bare requirements: conversations.md:5 'Our clients ask several things at once, so answers have to stay with their question'; conversations.md:29 'Our internet in court is patchy. If the same message is sent twice because the first reply got lost, it must appear only once'; walls-and-retention.md:17 'A wall has to be airtight, because a leak is a professional-conduct problem for us'; integration.md:7 'That means everything sent today has the same time, which is why we care that the order stays consistent.' Spec-like elements are bounded and justified: the accounts table (walls-and-retention.md:5-11) is necessary seed/login information, and integration.md:3 names Node 22, port 3000, Express/better-sqlite3 via NODE_PATH, DB_PATH and GET /api/health, which is the shared runtime contract required by check 4 rather than an implementation recipe (no routes, schema, components or framework for the UI are dictated). Enumerations such as the wall leak surfaces (walls-and-retention.md:17) are written as prose sentences explaining a business risk, not a checklist. Adversarial check: a stub/recipe-follower cannot exploit naturalness here (that is check 7's domain), and a conforming alternative (any UI framework, any API shape) is not excluded by recipe-like wording, since the brief prescribes outcomes, not structure. Mild observation, not a defect: the notes are dense with precise thresholds ('at least three levels deep' conversations.md:5, 'about 390 px' conversations.md:33, 'within about five seconds' conversations.md:31), which edge toward requirement density, but each is phrased conversationally with a reason and lives in the supporting notes, not the prompt. This row needs no runtime evidence; raw-evidence-index is not relevant to it.
